newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end mixed,interest seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end mixed,interest seen picking up.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in slower trade on Friday, with hoteliers posting new gains and headline shares weakening, but traders said they expected interest to increase next week due to a correction in prices.
Food processor Podravka was the only stock that really kept the market going, said Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest brokerage.
It added 3 kuna (49 cents) to 298, selling 1,332 shares after trading at 305 earlier in the week. Ilic said it could yet go a bit further down.
"Unlike other stocks Podravka had a large volume but its price had been corrected," he said.

This could encourage market activity next week, Ilic added. "The low prices could make the stocks interesting to investors. I think the decline (of prices) may stop next week and the market will stabilise."

Of the two blue chips, drugs firm Pliva held its ground at 472 kuna on a modest volume of 196 shares, while Zagrebacka Banka's ordinary stock fell 23 kuna to close at 2,077 with 735 shares changing hands.
The bank's bearer stock also shed 10 kuna to 800, selling only 2 shares but its preferred stock was the day's most active issue, gaining 6 kuna to 1,100 on volume of 1,583 shares.
Eight of 18 active issues rose, six fell and four were flat.

Riviera Porec led the hoteliers, adding 5 kuna to 155, on volume of 453. Other gainers included Jadranturist, Arenaturist and Suncani Hvar. Of active hoteliers only Laguna Porec was on the losing side, down 10 kuna to 1,420 on volume of 125 shares.
The day's biggest gainer was textile firm Varteks, which recovered some of Thursday's losses, adding five kuna or six percent to 85, on volume of 60 shares.
Friday's largest decliner was shipper Atlantska Plovidba, which lost 8 kuna or 6.7 percent to 102 from two weeks ago, on volume of 50 shares. ($ = 6.084 Croatian Kuna)
